claims.text: Controlled annealing can create a targeted nanoscale precipitate distribution in the rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy.
Controlled annealing can refine grain boundaries in the rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy.
Nanoscale precipitates act as nucleation sites for magnetostructural transitions.
Refined grain boundaries act as nucleation sites for magnetostructural transitions.
Annealing-induced nanoscale structural heterogeneity enhances local exchange interactions.
Annealing-induced nanoscale structural heterogeneity enhances local magnetostructural coupling.
Enhanced local exchange interactions and magnetostructural coupling increase magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
Distributed phase-transformation behavior avoids a large increase in hysteresis.
The tailored heterogeneous microstructure maintains kinetics sufficient for rapid heat exchange.
The annealed alloy will have a higher low-field magnetic entropy change than the untreated baseline.
The annealed alloy will not exhibit a significant increase in thermal hysteresis relative to the untreated baseline.
The annealing treatment will not compromise mechanical stability relative to the untreated baseline.
The untreated or conventionally treated alloy has a lower low-field magnetocaloric effect than the proposed annealed alloy.
The hypothesis applies across rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy compositions in which annealing induces beneficial nanoscale heterogeneity.
Excessive coarsening limits the beneficial response.
Phase separation that degrades mechanical integrity lies outside the hypothesis's valid processing range.
Unwanted magnetic ordering limits the beneficial response.
The magnitude of magnetocaloric improvement depends on the nanostructural changes induced by annealing.
